summary: This work proposes stroboscopic stabilization of cat qubits via repeated interactions with an auxiliary two-level system mediated by quadratic Hamiltonians, eliminating the need for engineered two-photon dissipation. The protocol preserves the noise bias, extends to squeezed cat qubits with partial single-photon-loss correction, and is compatible with trapped-ion and circuit-QED platforms.
motivation: Existing cat-qubit implementations rely on two-photon dissipation via nonlinear couplings to lossy reservoirs, limiting scalability and platform compatibility. A stabilization scheme without reservoir engineering would overcome these constraints and enable broader experimental implementations.
method: The authors derive stroboscopic stabilization sequences (small-Big-small, Sharpen-Trim, Big-small-Big) from a modular dissipator $d_\Delta^\mu$ using Suzuki-Trotter decompositions, implemented via conditional displacements $\mathrm{CD}(\alpha)$ and qubit rotations. The stabilizer operator $S_\Delta = -\exp[\pi(i\hat{q} - \Delta^2\hat{p})/2\alpha]$ has period $2\sqrt{2}\alpha$ and fixes $\Gamma\delta t = \Delta\pi/2\sqrt{2}\alpha$ for modularity.
result: Simulations show exponential bit-flip suppression $\Gamma_Z \sim \exp(-c|\beta_\mathrm{eff}|^2)$ with $c \approx 3$ for the small-Big-small sequence at $\alpha \gg 1$. For squeezed cat qubits with $r=0.4$ and $\kappa_- \delta t = 10^{-3}$, bit-flip rates reach $\approx 10^{-6}$ at $n_\mathrm{bar} \approx 4$, with phase-flip rates partially suppressed by squeezing and auxiliary-qubit dephasing contributing linearly at low rates ($\gamma_\phi/\kappa_- = 1$).
